task: This is a synthetic newspaper-writing exercise using fictional reporting notes. Use only the supplied reporting notes. Write from the reporting snapshot as of August 17, 2026. Write a headline and a 450–650-word AP-style newspaper explainer answering why a ticket at the Fernwick Playhouse now shows a higher initial price online even though the mandatory checkout total has not changed.

facts.text: Fernwick Playhouse changed its online price display on Aug. 10, 2026, for its autumn production of the original fictional play The Narrow Orchard.
An online ticket previously displayed a $30 base price before adding a $3 booking fee and a $2 facility charge.
The website now initially displays $35, the same mandatory total charged online before the display change.
The stated total includes all mandatory charges in the supplied price schedule; optional purchases are separate.
Buying at the playhouse counter avoids the $3 online booking fee but still carries the $2 facility charge, for a $32 total.
The counter opens Tuesday through Saturday from noon to 5 p.m., which is not convenient for every customer.
An optional $5 donation is offered at checkout but is not automatically selected.
Digital delivery is free; customers choosing postal delivery pay an additional $2 per order, not per ticket.
The facility charge goes into the playhouse's building fund, which is paying for roof work.
The booking fee pays the contracted ticketing provider and does not pass directly to performers.
The August 10–16, 2026, sales report records 300 online tickets and 180 counter tickets across multiple performance dates for this production.
Those tickets generated $16,260 in mandatory ticket receipts, excluding optional donations and postal delivery.
Playhouse manager Leda Voss said the aim of the display change is to make the first number closer to what the customer must pay.
Voss said, "The price has not gone up at checkout. We have stopped making people reach checkout to discover it."
Customer Toma Reed said comparing shows was difficult when one venue advertised totals and another advertised base prices.
Reed said, "I cannot compare two nights out if one number is a ticket and the other is only the start of one."
The playhouse has not published evidence that the new display increased sales or reduced abandoned orders.
Its stated cancellation policy returns mandatory ticket charges when the playhouse cancels a performance; ordinary customer cancellations follow separate terms.
The playhouse seats 240 people and uses numbered paper tickets for customers without email.
The supplied record describes this venue's practices, not a finding that every ticket seller follows the same fee or refund rules.

forbidden_additions: A $5 increase in the online mandatory total caused by the display change
Postal fees charged per ticket, an automatic donation or identical refund rules for all cancellations
